learning_outcomes.text: Has elementary knowledge about the relationships between social processes, structures, and institutions. Also knows the general relationships between processes occurring in society and culture and the formation of sociological ideas and theories.

Is able to present and interpret the processes of social institution changes against the background of social changes. Also has the ability to apply acquired knowledge to analyze changes occurring in Poland and the contemporary world, especially in the context of globalization changes.
Is also aware of the importance of sociological analysis for understanding contemporary social, political, economic, and cultural processes.
Is open to criticism of their arguments and can modify them as a result of discussion.

syllabus_topics: Society, sociology as a science, sociological theories.
Social institutions and problems (family, social control, religion).
Culture and tradition (cultural capital and functions of tradition).
Power, social differentiation, capitalism, social conflicts.
Social variability and visions of history.
Axiological instability of society and institutional order.
assessment_rules: Learning outcomes are verified by a test and activity during classes. Students participate in classes, learning subsequent teaching content according to the course syllabus. Students should ask questions and clarify doubts on an ongoing basis.
